tiers.name: syntax
tiers.goal: Type the language without thinking about it.

tiers.name: data
tiers.goal: Know what a value actually is in memory.

tiers.name: organization
tiers.goal: Structure code so it survives being changed.

tiers.name: runtime
tiers.goal: Know what the machine does while your code runs.

tiers.name: patterns
tiers.goal: Recognize the shape of a problem, then pick the idiomatic answer.

variants.name: var with explicit type
variants.when: you want the zero value, or the type is not obvious from the right-hand side

variants.name: short declaration
variants.when: inside a function where the value makes the type obvious

variants.name: naked returns
variants.when: short functions where the names document the result

variants.name: explicit returns
variants.when: anything long enough that you lose track of what is named

variants.name: value receivers
variants.when: small immutable types where copying is cheap and safe

variants.name: pointer receivers
variants.when: mutation, large structs, or any type with a mutex

variants.name: mixed receivers
variants.when: almost never — it confuses the method set rules

variants.name: accept interfaces, return structs
variants.when: library code that must stay flexible for callers

variants.name: small single-method interfaces
variants.when: testing seams and composition, the Go default

variants.name: large service interfaces
variants.when: rarely right; usually a Java habit leaking in

variants.name: sentinel errors
variants.when: callers must test for one specific known failure: errors.Is

variants.name: typed errors
variants.when: callers need structured data off the failure: errors.As

variants.name: opaque wrapped errors
variants.when: the caller only logs it; keeps your internals private

variants.name: Result-style generic type
variants.when: forces handling at the type level, fights every stdlib signature

variants.name: panic and recover
variants.when: truly unrecoverable invariants, and package boundaries only

variants.name: generic function
variants.when: the same algorithm over many types, checked at compile time

variants.name: interface parameter
variants.when: behaviour varies per type; dynamic dispatch is the point

variants.name: any plus type switch
variants.when: few known types, and you want them all in one place

variants.name: code generation
variants.when: you need per-type optimisation the compiler will not give you

variants.name: channels
variants.when: transferring ownership of data between goroutines

variants.name: mutex over shared state
variants.when: protecting a struct field; usually simpler than a channel

variants.name: errgroup
variants.when: fan-out where the first failure should cancel the rest

variants.name: worker pool
variants.when: bounded concurrency over an unbounded queue of work

variants.name: struct tags
variants.when: the default; declarative and enough for most payloads

variants.name: custom MarshalJSON
variants.when: the wire format genuinely differs from your struct

variants.name: intermediate DTO type
variants.when: the API contract must not move when the domain type does

variants.name: code generation
variants.when: hot paths where reflection cost actually shows in a profile

variants.name: functional options
variants.when: many optional settings, and the API must stay additive

variants.name: config struct
variants.when: few settings, all known up front; far less machinery

variants.name: builder with method chaining
variants.when: rare in Go; reads well but hides the error path

variants.name: variadic plain args
variants.when: two or three options that will never grow

variants.name: repository interface
variants.when: you need to swap or fake the store in tests

variants.name: direct queries in the service
variants.when: small services where the indirection buys nothing

variants.name: query object
variants.when: complex read paths that do not fit a CRUD-shaped interface

haskell.title: Values and Types
mechanism: a binding is a definition, not a slot — there is nothing to overwrite and no zero value
Hindley-Milner infers the most general type; a signature narrows it
numeric literals are polymorphic, resolved by fromInteger at the use site
type identity is nominal — a newtype over Int is not an Int

variants.name: top-level type signature
variants.when: always at the top level — it is documentation the compiler checks, and it pins the monomorphism restriction

variants.name: inferred, no signature
variants.when: a local binding in a where or let where the type is obvious and noisy to write

variants.name: newtype wrapper
variants.when: the value needs its own identity so the compiler rejects mixing it with a bare Int

haskell.title: Operators and Expressions
mechanism: operators are ordinary functions; `div` in backticks and (+) in parens are the same thing
infixl/infixr fixity declarations are what actually drive parsing
$ is function application at the lowest precedence, so it deletes trailing parens
sections partially apply an operator: (2^) and (^2) are different functions

variants.name: parentheses
variants.when: a short expression where nesting is obvious at a glance

variants.name: $ application
variants.when: one deeply nested call where the closing paren pile would be the only hard part to read

variants.name: (.) composition
variants.when: you are naming a pipeline of transformations rather than applying one now

haskell.title: Control Flow
mechanism: if is an expression and both branches are mandatory — there is no statement to fall off
guards and pattern matches both compile down to case
case forces the scrutinee to weak head normal form, which is where evaluation actually happens
where scopes over a whole equation including its guards; let scopes over one expression

variants.name: pattern match
variants.when: dispatching on the shape of a value — the compiler can then check exhaustiveness

variants.name: guards
variants.when: dispatching on a predicate over an already-matched value

variants.name: if-then-else
variants.when: exactly two outcomes and no structure to destructure

haskell.title: Functions
mechanism: every function takes exactly one argument — currying is the calling convention, not a feature
partial application therefore needs no special support; a -> b -> c is a -> (b -> c)
eta reduction and where point-free style stops paying for itself
lambdas close over the environment; GHC allocates a closure for the captured free variables

variants.name: explicit arguments
variants.when: the argument names carry meaning the types do not

variants.name: point-free
variants.when: a short composition where naming the argument adds nothing

variants.name: named helper in where
variants.when: the sub-expression is used twice, or deserves a name for the reader

haskell.title: Lists and Folds
mechanism: a list is a lazy chain of cons cells, not an array — indexing is O(n) and there is no bounds check to skip
foldr builds structure lazily and works on infinite lists; foldl' consumes strictly and works on long ones
foldl without the bang builds a chain of thunks and is the classic Haskell space leak
map and filter fuse into a single loop under -O, so the intermediate list is never allocated

variants.name: foldr
variants.when: the combining function is lazy in its second argument, or the input may be infinite

variants.name: foldl'
variants.when: reducing a long finite list to a single strict value

variants.name: explicit recursion
variants.when: the traversal is irregular enough that a fold obscures it

variants.name: library combinator
variants.when: the operation already has a name — sum, any, partition — and reimplementing it is noise

haskell.title: Strings and Text
mechanism: String is a type alias for [Char] — a linked list of boxed characters, one cons cell per letter
Data.Text is a packed UTF-8 array with O(1) length and real slicing
ByteString is bytes with no encoding attached; treating it as text is where mojibake comes from
OverloadedStrings makes a literal polymorphic via fromString, chosen by the expected type

variants.name: String
variants.when: a tiny amount of text, or an interface you do not control that already speaks String

variants.name: Data.Text
variants.when: any real text handling — it is the default for anything user-facing

variants.name: ByteString
variants.when: bytes off a socket or a file where you have not decided the encoding yet

haskell.title: Algebraic Data Types
mechanism: sum and product types make cardinality literal arithmetic: Either a b is |a| + |b|, (a, b) is |a| * |b|
constructors are ordinary functions, so Just is a function of type a -> Maybe a
newtype is erased at runtime; data allocates a box and adds a layer of laziness
record syntax generates field accessors that are partial when the type has several constructors

variants.name: data with positional constructors
variants.when: two or three fields whose order is obvious from the type

variants.name: data with record syntax
variants.when: enough fields that positions stop being readable, and you want update syntax

variants.name: newtype
variants.when: exactly one field, and you want the type distinction with no runtime cost

variants.name: type alias
variants.when: you are shortening a signature, not making a new type — no safety is added

haskell.title: Laziness and Thunks
mechanism: a binding is a thunk — an unevaluated closure — until something demands its value
weak head normal form means the outermost constructor only; NF means all the way down
seq, bang patterns and strict constructor fields are the three ways to force
a space leak is an unforced accumulator: the thunk chain is retained instead of the number

variants.name: lazy by default
variants.when: the value may not be needed, or the structure is infinite or streaming

variants.name: bang pattern
variants.when: forcing one accumulator inside a loop or fold

variants.name: strict fields in the data type
variants.when: the record is a state value that should never hold a thunk

variants.name: deepseq / force
variants.when: pushing evaluation across a boundary — before timing, or before handing work to another thread

haskell.title: Modules and Imports
mechanism: one module per file; the export list is the only thing that makes a name private
qualified imports avoid clashes without renaming, which is why Data.Map is always qualified
the Prelude is an implicit unqualified import you can hide from or replace
modules are a namespace and a compilation unit; packages are the dependency boundary

variants.name: open import
variants.when: the module is designed to be imported wholesale, like a Prelude replacement

variants.name: qualified import
variants.when: the module exports names that collide with the Prelude — Map, Text, ByteString

variants.name: explicit import list
variants.when: you want the reader to see exactly which names arrived from where

haskell.title: Typeclasses
mechanism: a class is a record of functions — a dictionary — that GHC passes implicitly at the call site
instances are selected by type at compile time, never by a value at runtime
coherence: one instance per type globally, which is why orphan instances are a problem
deriving generates the instance mechanically; Functor and Generic go through the type's shape

variants.name: typeclass
variants.when: the behaviour genuinely belongs to the type and there is one right instance for it

variants.name: record of functions
variants.when: the caller must be able to choose or swap the implementation at runtime

variants.name: plain function parameter
variants.when: one behaviour varies in one place and a class would be ceremony

haskell.title: Errors
mechanism: Maybe and Either are ordinary values — failure is data the type system forces you to look at
exceptions still exist, are untyped at the throw site, and can arrive asynchronously from another thread
error and undefined are bottoms that inhabit every type, which is how they typecheck anywhere
ExceptT stacks a failure channel onto another monad and changes what short-circuits

variants.name: Maybe
variants.when: absence with exactly one cause, where naming it would add nothing

variants.name: Either e a
variants.when: an expected failure the caller must distinguish and handle

variants.name: ExceptT over IO
variants.when: a pipeline of effectful steps that should stop at the first failure

variants.name: throwIO / Control.Exception
variants.when: genuinely exceptional, or crossing an IO boundary that already speaks exceptions

variants.name: error / bottom
variants.when: an invariant that cannot be false — a bug, not a failure mode

haskell.title: Parametric Polymorphism
mechanism: parametricity: a -> a has exactly one total implementation, so a signature constrains behaviour
kinds classify types — Int has kind Type, Maybe has kind Type -> Type
a constraint is a dictionary argument, so Ord a => a -> a is a function of two arguments underneath
rank-2 types need an explicit forall because inference cannot guess where to generalise

variants.name: fully parametric
variants.when: the function does not care what the value is — the widest, most provable signature

variants.name: constrained
variants.when: you need one capability, and the constraint documents exactly which

variants.name: concrete type
variants.when: the function is genuinely about that type and generality would be speculative

haskell.title: Evaluation and Memory
mechanism: GHC compiles to STG and evaluates by graph reduction — a thunk is overwritten in place once forced
boxed Int is a pointer to a heap object; Int# is the machine word, and unboxing is what -O buys you
the generational GC is tuned for very high allocation of very short-lived objects
reading +RTS -s: allocation rate, copied bytes, and productivity are the three numbers that matter

haskell.title: IO and the Runtime
mechanism: IO a is a description of an effect, an inert value — nothing happens until the runtime runs it
main is the single IO value the RTS executes; everything else is reachable from it or dead
do notation is sugar for >>= and >>, and desugars identically for every monad
unsafePerformIO breaks referential transparency and exists for FFI and top-level caches

haskell.title: Concurrency
mechanism: forkIO makes a green thread: a few hundred bytes and microseconds, scheduled by the RTS onto capabilities
MVar is a mutex and a one-slot box at once; an empty MVar blocks the reader
STM composes — two correct transactions combine into a correct one, which locks never do
async ties a thread's lifetime to a scope and rethrows its exception in the waiter

variants.name: MVar
variants.when: one piece of mutable state with one owner at a time

variants.name: STM / TVar
variants.when: several pieces of state that must change together, or a retry condition

variants.name: Chan / TQueue
variants.when: handing work between producer and consumer threads

variants.name: forkIO alone
variants.when: fire-and-forget work whose failure genuinely does not matter — rare, and usually a bug

haskell.title: Serialization
mechanism: a decoder is a total function from bytes to Either error a — parse failure is a value, not an exception
the usual shape is a Value ADT built first, then converted into your own type
generic deriving walks the type's shape at compile time via GHC.Generics and costs compile time, not runtime
encoding is a fold to a Builder, which appends in O(1) instead of concatenating strings

variants.name: hand-written encoder and parser
variants.when: a small, fixed format where the dependency is not worth it

variants.name: generic deriving
variants.when: the wire shape matches the Haskell type and you want it to stay in sync automatically

variants.name: explicit instances
variants.when: the wire format is fixed by someone else and does not match your field names

haskell.title: Functor, Applicative, Monad
mechanism: one abstraction at three strengths: map over a context, combine independent contexts, sequence dependent ones
the laws are not trivia — they are what makes refactoring a pipeline safe
do notation is monad-agnostic sugar; the same block works for Maybe, Either, IO and lists
Applicative can collect every error because the steps are independent; Monad short-circuits at the first

variants.name: fmap
variants.when: one value in a context, one transformation, no failure to combine

variants.name: Applicative style
variants.when: several independent pieces — validating a config where you want every error, not the first

variants.name: Monad / do notation
variants.when: a later step needs the result of an earlier one

variants.name: traverse
variants.when: you have a container of values and an effectful function, and want the effect outside

haskell.title: Monad Transformers
mechanism: a transformer adds one capability to a monad underneath: StateT s IO is state on top of IO
lift moves an action one layer up the stack, which is the boilerplate mtl exists to remove
mtl removes the lifts with typeclasses at the cost of n-squared instances and worse error messages
ReaderT env IO is the shape most production Haskell converges on, because it stays inspectable

variants.name: ReaderT over IO
variants.when: an application with configuration and effects — the default production choice

variants.name: concrete transformer stack
variants.when: a small, self-contained computation where naming the stack is clearer than abstracting it

variants.name: mtl-style constraints
variants.when: you want each function to declare only the capabilities it actually uses

variants.name: no transformer at all
variants.when: passing the argument explicitly is shorter than the machinery to hide it

haskell.title: Smart Constructors and Illegal States
mechanism: hiding a constructor from the export list is the entire enforcement mechanism — there is no other access
newtype plus a validating function moves a runtime check to a place that runs once
making illegal states unrepresentable trades a class of test for a class of type
the cost is real: wrapping, unwrapping, and a constructor you now have to maintain

variants.name: smart constructor
variants.when: the invariant is cheap to check once and expensive to re-check everywhere

variants.name: restructure the type
variants.when: the illegal state can be designed out entirely — the strictly better fix when available

variants.name: validate at the boundary
variants.when: the value comes from outside and the inside can then assume it is good

haskell.title: Parser Combinators
mechanism: a parser is a function from input to a result plus the rest of the input, wrapped in a monad
the combinators are ordinary values, so the grammar is a first-class thing you can build and reuse
backtracking is explicit — try is what makes an alternative reconsider consumed input
the Applicative parts of a grammar can be analysed statically; the Monad parts cannot

variants.name: parser combinators
variants.when: a grammar with structure — nesting, recursion, or good error messages needed

variants.name: hand-written recursive descent
variants.when: a hot path where you need control over allocation and backtracking

variants.name: splitting on delimiters
variants.when: the format is genuinely flat and a parser would be over-engineering

haskell.title: Functional Core, Imperative Shell
mechanism: IO lives at the edges; the middle is pure functions that are trivially testable
a record of functions passed in is dependency injection with no framework
a typeclass-per-effect moves the choice to compile time and out of the call site
the boundary is where you decide what is a value and what is an effect — everything downstream follows

variants.name: handle / record of functions
variants.when: the implementation is chosen at runtime — a real one and a fake for tests

variants.name: typeclass constraint per effect
variants.when: each function should declare which effects it can perform

variants.name: plain pure functions plus IO at main
variants.when: the program is small enough that a seam would be speculative

haskell.title: Effect Systems
mechanism: a free monad turns commands into a data structure that an interpreter walks later
extensible effects put an open union of effects in one type parameter
modern libraries compile back down to ReaderT over IO, so the runtime cost is mostly gone
the cost that remains is type inference and the size of the error message when it fails

variants.name: ReaderT over IO
variants.when: you want effects to be obvious and the stack trace to stay readable

variants.name: mtl constraints
variants.when: capability-per-function typing without adopting a new library

variants.name: free monad
variants.when: the program must be inspected or reinterpreted — multiple backends, or a test interpreter

variants.name: algebraic effect library
variants.when: a large application where the effect set changes often and the boilerplate has become the cost

python.title: Values and Types
mechanism: everything is an object with a refcount
names bind, they do not store

python.title: Control Flow
mechanism: no block scope, only function scope

python.title: Functions
mechanism: default args evaluate once at def time

python.title: Lists, Dicts, Sets
mechanism: dicts are compact and insertion ordered

python.title: Strings
mechanism: str is immutable and sometimes interned

variants.name: plain class
variants.when: behaviour and invariants matter more than the data

variants.name: dataclass
variants.when: records with some behaviour; the default for most value types

variants.name: NamedTuple
variants.when: immutable, tuple-compatible, cheap

variants.name: TypedDict
variants.when: the data is already a dict and must stay one, such as JSON

python.title: Modules and Packages
mechanism: the import system and sys.modules cache

variants.name: Protocol
variants.when: structural typing; the implementer need not know about you

variants.name: ABC
variants.when: you want registration and an explicit inheritance relationship

variants.name: duck typing with no annotation
variants.when: internal code where the contract is obvious

variants.name: raise an exception
variants.when: the Python default; failures propagate until someone cares

variants.name: return None
variants.when: one failure mode, and the caller will obviously check

variants.name: Result type
variants.when: you want the type checker to force handling; fights the ecosystem

variants.name: exception groups
variants.when: concurrent work where several things can fail at once

python.title: Memory and GC
mechanism: reference counting is the primary mechanism
the cycle collector handles the rest

python.title: Concurrency and asyncio
mechanism: the GIL and what it does not protect
the event loop and coroutine scheduling

variants.name: asyncio
variants.when: many concurrent I/O waits in one thread

variants.name: threads
variants.when: blocking I/O in libraries that are not async-aware

variants.name: multiprocessing
variants.when: CPU-bound work under the GIL

variants.name: free-threaded build
variants.when: 3.14 onward; real threads for CPU work, ecosystem still catching up

variants.name: function decorator
variants.when: cross-cutting behaviour with no state

variants.name: class decorator
variants.when: you need to modify the type itself

variants.name: context manager
variants.when: the concern is setup and teardown around a block

variants.name: explicit wrapper call
variants.when: the indirection would hide something the reader needs

scala.title: Values and Types
mechanism: everything is an object, including Int
val is a stable reference, not deep immutability
Any, AnyVal, AnyRef and the unified hierarchy

variants.name: val
variants.when: the default — a binding that will not be reassigned

variants.name: var
variants.when: genuinely mutating local state, and almost nowhere else

variants.name: lazy val
variants.when: expensive to compute and possibly never needed

variants.name: def
variants.when: recomputed on every access; no memoisation

scala.title: Operators and Expressions
mechanism: right-associative methods end in a colon

scala.title: Control Flow
mechanism: if and match are expressions that return values

scala.title: Functions
mechanism: eta-expansion turns a method into a function

scala.title: Collections
mechanism: List is a linked list, Vector is a trie
views are lazy, iterators are single-use

variants.name: List
variants.when: sequential access, pattern matching, prepend-heavy work

variants.name: Vector
variants.when: random access and append; the general-purpose default

variants.name: Array
variants.when: interop with Java, or primitives without boxing

variants.name: LazyList
variants.when: infinite or expensive sequences consumed partially

scala.title: Strings
mechanism: s, f and raw interpolators are compile-time

scala.title: Classes and Objects
mechanism: case classes generate equals, hashCode, copy and unapply
companion objects hold what would be statics
enums in 3 replace sealed trait hierarchies

variants.name: case class
variants.when: immutable data with structural equality; the default

variants.name: plain class
variants.when: identity matters, or you control equality yourself

variants.name: enum
variants.when: a closed set of alternatives — 3's replacement for sealed traits

variants.name: opaque type
variants.when: a zero-cost wrapper that stops a String being any String

scala.title: References and Mutation
mechanism: val prevents reassignment, not mutation of the referent

scala.title: Modules and Packages
mechanism: given instances are found by scope, not import alone

scala.title: Traits and Given
mechanism: type classes are given instances plus extension methods

variants.name: trait
variants.when: shared behaviour an implementer opts into by extending

variants.name: given instance
variants.when: type class evidence supplied at the call site

variants.name: abstract class
variants.when: you need constructor parameters and single inheritance is fine

variants.name: plain function parameter
variants.when: when the indirection buys nothing over passing it

scala.title: Errors
mechanism: exceptions are unchecked on the JVM
Either and Try are values, not control flow

variants.name: Either
variants.when: expected failures with a typed error the caller must handle

variants.name: Try
variants.when: wrapping code that throws, especially Java interop

variants.name: Option
variants.when: absence with no explanation needed

variants.name: throw
variants.when: truly exceptional; the caller is not expected to recover

variants.name: effect type such as IO
variants.when: errors, resources and concurrency handled as one thing

scala.title: Generics
mechanism: context bounds desugar to using parameters
match types compute types from types

scala.title: Concurrency
mechanism: Future needs an ExecutionContext in scope
Future is eager, IO is not
virtual threads change the blocking calculus

variants.name: Future
variants.when: simple async on the stdlib with no dependency

variants.name: cats-effect IO
variants.when: referentially transparent effects, cancellation, resource safety

variants.name: ZIO
variants.when: typed errors and dependencies baked into the effect

variants.name: virtual threads
variants.when: JDK 21 onward; blocking code that no longer costs a thread

scala.title: Serialization
mechanism: no JSON in the standard library

variants.name: circe
variants.when: the common choice; derivation plus a rich combinator API

variants.name: upickle
variants.when: less ceremony and fewer dependencies

variants.name: jsoniter-scala
variants.when: hot paths where allocation actually shows in a profile

variants.name: hand-written codecs
variants.when: the wire format and the domain type genuinely diverge

variants.name: case class with defaults
variants.when: the usual answer; named arguments do the work

variants.name: builder
variants.when: a long construction sequence with validation at the end

variants.name: phantom-typed builder
variants.when: the compiler should reject an incomplete build

variants.name: class
variants.when: identity, inheritance, or instanceof checks actually matter

variants.name: factory function with closures
variants.when: true privacy and no this binding to get wrong

variants.name: plain object plus functions
variants.when: data and behaviour are genuinely separate

variants.name: interface
variants.when: object contracts meant to be extended or augmented

variants.name: type alias
variants.when: unions, intersections, mapped and conditional types

variants.name: branded type
variants.when: you need nominal typing so UserId cannot be an OrderId

variants.name: throw
variants.when: exceptional paths the caller is not expected to handle locally

variants.name: Result union type
variants.when: expected failures you want the compiler to force you to handle

variants.name: discriminated union on a status field
variants.when: several outcomes, not just ok and error

variants.name: null or undefined return
variants.when: one failure mode with no useful detail

variants.name: generic function
variants.when: one implementation across many types

variants.name: function overloads
variants.when: the return type depends on the argument in a non-generic way

variants.name: conditional types
variants.when: the type must be computed from another type

variants.name: async and await
variants.when: the default; sequential-looking code with real error boundaries

variants.name: promise combinators
variants.when: concurrent work: all, allSettled, race, any

variants.name: async iterators
variants.when: streams and paginated sources

variants.name: callbacks
variants.when: legacy interop only

variants.name: JSON.parse plus a type assertion
variants.when: fast and unsafe; you are trusting the source

variants.name: runtime schema validation
variants.when: any external boundary; the assertion is a lie without it

variants.name: hand-written type guards
variants.when: few shapes, no dependency wanted
